A Flutter developer is a software engineer who uses Google's open-source UI toolkit to create natively compiled applications for mobile (iOS, Android), web, and desktop from a single codebase. description:
A full-stack developer is a versatile software engineer proficient in building both the front-end (user-facing) and back-end (server, database) components of web applications.
 They manage the entire development lifecycle, from designing user interfaces to implementing server logic, managing databases, and integrating APIs. Common technologies include JavaScript, React, Node.js, Python, and SQL. 
Key Responsibilities & Skills:
Front-End: Developing client-side interfaces using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and frameworks like React, Vue, or Angular.
Back-End: Building server-side logic using languages such as Python, PHP, Java, or Node.js.
Database Management: Working with SQL (MySQL, PostgreSQL) or NoSQL (MongoDB) databases.
API & Server: Designing and consuming RESTful APIs and managing server environments.
Version Control: Using tools like Git for code collaboration. 

Advantages of Full-Stack Developers:
Versatility: Capable of handling multiple stages of development, which is ideal for creating MVPs (Minimum Viable Products).
Efficiency: Ability to switch between front-end and back-end tasks streamlines the development process.
Problem Solving: A holistic view of the application allows for better debugging and, system optimization. 

How to Become a Full-Stack Developer?:
Education: A degree in Computer Science or related fields is common, though not always required.
Learning Path: Mastering HTML/CSS/JS, learning a back-end language (e.g., Python/Node.js), understanding databases, and using frameworks.
Projects: Building practical applications to gain hands-on experience and build a portfolio. 

Career Outlook:
Demand: High demand due to their ability to work across the entire stack.
Salary: In India, salaries for full-stack developers are competitive, with reported averages around ₹8,48,631 per year.
Roles: Often involved in Agile or lean development environments, working on everything from planning to final deployment.

Key Responsibilities & Skills:
Development: Writing, testing, and debugging high-quality, efficient code throughout the software development life cycle (SDLC).
Technologies: Proficiency in Core Java, JVM, Spring Boot, Microservices, and database interaction (SQL/ORM tools).
Problem Solving: Analyzing user requirements, identifying system vulnerabilities, and implementing technical solutions.
Collaboration: Working with teams to integrate frontend components (Angular, React) with backend logic, often in full-stack roles. 

Job Market & Roles:
Demand: High demand for Java developers, including roles like Java Backend Developer, Full Stack Developer, and Technical Lead, with numerous opportunities at firms like TCS, Capgemini, Infosys, and Morgan Stanley.
Experience Levels: Opportunities range from freshers/junior roles to senior positions requiring 5-10+ years of experience.
Salary: Average salary for a Java developer in India is approximately ₹6.7 Lakhs per year, with experienced professionals at companies like TCS earning significantly higher. 

Common Qualifications:
Degree in Computer Science or related field.
Proficiency in Java 8 or higher, plus modern frameworks.
Strong understanding of object-oriented programming (OOP) principles and design patterns.

Access Control: Managing user accounts and permissions.
